newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian ruling parties back new finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Latvian ruling parties back new finance minister.

text.p: Latvia's ruling government parties on Wednesday backed the candidature of Robert Zile as new finance minister, officials said.

The eight parties that form the government led by Prime Minister Andris Shkele decided at their regular meeting to back Zile, who has been picked from the third-largest party, For Fatherland and Freedom.

"The government parties unanimously supported the candidature of Robert Zile and parliament is almost definitely going to vote on his approval on Thursday," the head of the Latvia's Way parliament faction, Andrej Panteleev, told Reuters.
Latvia's Way is the second-largest party in the government.
Zile's election as finance minister was made almost certain on Tuesday after largest party, the Democratic Party Saimnieks, said it supported him.
Zile, 38, is currently head of the parliament budget and finance committee.
He is an economist by profession but has been in politics since the late 1980s when the movement began to regain Latvia's independence from the Soviet Union.
He has also been on the board of leading bank Unibanka, Riga commercial port and the Latvian Privatisation Agency.
